newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks move lower in mid-week trade.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks move lower in mid-week trade.

text.p: The Cyprus stockmarket moved sluggishly in the first two trading sessions this week, slipping 0.90 percent in listless trading.

The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) general share index, which is set at 100 points, closed at 81.72 points on Wednesday after opening at 82.43. The market was closed on Tuesday, a Cypriot public holiday marking independence day.
The all-share index closed on Friday at 82.47.

Stocks on the market have lost 8.15 percent of their value since September 4. Floor traders have attributed the drop to lower-than-expected half-yearly results announced by some listed companies last month and investors waiting in the sidelines for more results expected out next week.
Losses were posted in all seven sub-indices. The banking sub-index closed at 88.86 points, shedding 0.64 points over Friday's close of 89.50.
Fully paid shares of the Bank of Cyprus closed unchanged at 339.5. Fully paid shares in the Cyprus Popular Bank closed at 313.5, down four cents from Friday.
Hellenic Bank fully paid shares closed at 246.5 from 250 on Friday.
The tourist company sub-index dropped to 73.42 on Wednesday, losing 3.37 percent in two days.

Tourism arrivals until mid-August are down four percent on corresponding figures for last year. The eastern Mediterranean island's economy depends heavily on tourism as its primary source of foreign exchange receipts and represents 21 percent of its GDP.
The insurance company sub-index closed at 60.09, down from 60.51 on Friday.
Universal Life Insurance closed higher at 380, up six cents from 374. Paneuropean Insurance, which is due to announce its six-monthly results next week, lost 4.5 cents and closed at 131.5.
Cyprus Airways, the island's state-controlled national carrier, was unchanged at 43 cents.
